destination.name: Hotel Okura Amsterdam
destination.note: No installed model or landmarks.json entry covered this pand; the OSM point n2817713466 exists in click-poi-info.json and is reused as landmarkId.

facts: Architects Bernard Bijvoet and Gerard Holt with the Japanese architects Yoshiro Taniguchi and Yozo Shibata; opened 24 September 1971 by Prince Claus; first European hotel of the Okura chain.
23 floors, 78 m; second-tallest building in Amsterdam at opening, after Toren Overhoeks; Ciel Bleu restaurant on the 23rd floor.
The lighting of the canopy ('luifel') at about 75 m is a weather barometer (blue sun, green bad weather, white changeable).

measuredBy.3dbag: NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012150422 LoD2.2: ground -0.575 m NAP, roofMax 79.7 m NAP, pand ground area 5078 m2. 3DBAG fuses the tower canopy overhang into full-height walls around a 41 x 35 m footprint and has no podium roof under it; those walls are cut to the podium height and the open loops capped in the builder.
measuredBy.towerFrame: 27.8 x 22.6 m rectangle rotated 4.95 degrees, NW corner (-4.1, -27.1) native east/south m from the BAG centroid, fitted to the 73.3 m roof-deck patches; canopy overhang 3.2 m, soffit 77.0 m, top 77.9 m.
measuredBy.facade: Y0 14.2 m to deck 73.3 m: 19 window storeys of about 3.1 m plus a glazed restaurant storey; 8 window axes on the north/south faces, 6 on the east/west faces (counted by eye on the 2016 and 2018 photos).
uncertain: Which faces are north/south of the photo views is deduced from the canal side (Amstelkanaal south of the hotel) and sun direction in the January 2016 photo.
North and east faces have no reference photo (inferred); the podium and the cantilevered lobby front are simplified 3DBAG massing with ribbon glazing, not photographed.
Window axis counts are mine, not blind-counted; the integrator's blind count may differ.
